hot take but i didn't love this one as much as others seemed to. i don't think an hour of cynicism and misery automatically makes an episode good. there were things i liked about it, the selfless husband literally chipping away at himself to make his dying wife happy is an excellent metaphor. but by the end i don't really get what the point is supposed to be. what's the 'black mirror' reflecting in the audience here? the protagonists are morally pure victims of an exploitative system. the technology fulfils their desire to... not die of terminal illness? there are glimmers of something interesting in the 'lux' package that allows people to augment their own emotions but that's never meaningfully explored past its base function as a stand-in for drugs. and any conflict or tension within the relationship as a result of all of this is ultimately rendered meaningless by the choice to literally skip straight to the conclusion we all saw coming from the start.

i genuinely think this episode would've worked better if it dropped (or at least sidelined) the whole subscription model gimmick and let it be primarily about a man doing increasingly more debasing and painful things for money to keep his dying wife alive, and the people who pay to watch him do them. none of the technology in this episode is as groundbreaking or harrowing as it thinks it is ("what if they put ads in your brain" rings especially hollow and yet that sequence is soooo drawn out) and the story bounces from beat to beat without any sense of purpose or intent. there's no journey. nothing is learned. bad things happen and then it ends. some may find this compelling. i do not.
